passages.provision_quote: B. Athletic teams or sports designated for "females", "women" or "girls" may not be open to students of the male sex. C. This section does not restrict the eligibility of any student to participate in any interscholastic or intramural athletic team or sport designated as being for "males", "men" or "boys" or designated as "coed" or "mixed".

rows.reasoning: Bolick co-sponsored SB 1165 (2022) and voted Y on its House Third Reading (31-24, so not near-unanimous), a single-subject bill whose operative section requires teams to be designated by biological sex and provides that teams "designated for "females", "women" or "girls" may not be open to students of the male sex". That is the rung requiring transgender athletes "to compete only on teams matching their biological sex assigned at birth". Subsection C leaves boys' and coed teams open to any student, which excludes the rung that bans transgender athletes from any organized sports competition.
